lyrics:
[Intro: palm-muted power chords, fast hi-hat count-in]

[Verse 1: earnest young male voice, fast]
Took the cash, took the car, said some things I can't take back
Told my dad he was dead to me, and I didn't even pack
Eighteen months of other people's couches, other people's fun
Woke up broke behind a diner, eating scraps. I was done.

[Pre-Chorus: half-time, building]
So I wrote a speech on a napkin, walking home
"I'm not your son. Just let me mow the lawn."

[Chorus: explosive, shouted melody, gang vocals]
And I was halfway down the driveway
With my speech in my hand
When the screen door blew wide open
And I saw my old man run
He never ran for anything, bad knee and all
Halfway down the driveway
He didn't let me finish. He didn't let me fall.

[Verse 2: fast, guitars wide open]
Put his jacket on my shoulders, yelled, "Fire up the grill!"
Called the neighbors, called the cousins, I was standing there still
My brother's in the garage, mad, and honestly, that's fair
But Dad just keeps on saying, "He was gone. He's here. He's here."

[Pre-Chorus: half-time, building]
Somebody told that story two thousand years ago
To show us what his Father's like. Now I know.

[Chorus: explosive, shouted melody, gang vocals]
And I was halfway down the driveway
With my speech in my hand
When the screen door blew wide open
And I saw my old man run
He never ran for anything, bad knee and all
Halfway down the driveway
He didn't let me finish. He didn't let me fall.

[Bridge: half-time, crowd chant]
Whoa-oh, I had a speech
Whoa-oh, he had a feast
Jesus said that's how God sees me
Running, running, running to me

[Final Chorus: fastest and loudest]
And I was halfway down the driveway
With my speech in my hand
When the screen door blew wide open
And I saw my Father run
He never stopped watching that road, not once
Halfway down the driveway
He didn't let me finish. He didn't let me fall.

[Outro: feedback, a screen door slam, spoken]
Welcome home, kid.
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 168 BPM, 4/4, E major. Fast, bright pop-punk with half-time drops before each chorus.

VOICE: Young male tenor, nasal, earnest and slightly strained, in the style of early-2000s pop-punk. He crams the verse words in quickly and shouts the choruses with a gang behind him. An older man speaks the last line.

INSTRUMENTS: Two overdriven guitars playing palm-muted power chords that open up in the chorus, a picked bass following the guitars, fast punk drums with a cracking snare, gang vocals, a little guitar feedback.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, muted chords and count-in. 0:08 Verse 1. 0:30 Pre-chorus, half-time. 0:40 Chorus 1. 1:02 Verse 2. 1:24 Pre-chorus, the old story. 1:34 Chorus 2. 1:56 Bridge, crowd chant. 2:16 Final chorus. 2:40 Outro, feedback, a door slam and the spoken line at 2:46.

PRODUCTION & MIX: 2003-style pop-punk: bright, tight, loud guitars panned wide, vocals doubled, nothing subtle.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: 'And I saw my old man run' at 0:48.

THE REVEAL: Until 1:24 it is a present-day boy coming home to his dad. The second pre-chorus says the story is two thousand years old and whose Father it describes; the bridge names Jesus as the teller, and the last chorus capitalises 'Father'.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Ashamed, rehearsing, overwhelmed, home.
